LESSON: CAPACITY (HOW MUCH A CONTAINER CAN HOLD)

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / PP1
Subject: General
Strand: MEASUREMENT
Topic 3.3: Capacity (how much a container can hold)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Capacity (how much a container can hold), part of MEASUREMENT in SNE  /  visual-impairment / PP1 General.

Key inquiry question: How many small containers can fill the big container?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Capacity (how much a container can hold) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking and problem solving: The learner finds out how many small containers can fill a big one.

Values:
• Responsibility: The learner fills and empties containers without spilling over water or sand.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Hygiene: The learner observes hygiene as they do emptying and filling activities (not to drink dirty water)

Link to other activity areas:

• Environmental activities: The learner uses natural resources of the environment like water and soil to fill

and empty containers.
